blocks.content: Course: Make Your Code Work on Every Screen
A media query is a CSS rule that only switches on when a certain condition is met.
In the Figma to Code course you wrote the hero like this for desktop.
Click Run Code and switch to mobile view. See what that looks like on a phone.
Not great, right? A portrait image and a block of text trying to sit side by side in 360px of space.
It would be so much nicer if on a phone the content just stacked. Portrait on top, text below, easy to read. So for mobile let's make it a single column.
Click Run Code and switch to mobile view. Much better.
But what about a tablet or desktop?
On those screens there's plenty of room. So what if we could say "if the screen is a tablet or bigger, go back to two columns"?
That's exactly what a media query does. A media query is for viewport width, the actual width of the browser window, not the device, not the font size, just how wide the screen is at that moment.
▶️ Next, let's see what that looks like in code.
